title: Categorize receipts and expenses for bookkeeping
summary: Paste receipt text and your chart of accounts; get a category, confidence, and a needs-review flag. You confirm before anything hits the books.

tests.prompt:
You are helping with bookkeeping. Categorize this expense against my chart of accounts.

Expense: [DESCRIPTION FROM RECEIPT OR EMAIL]
Amount: [AMOUNT] [CURRENCY]
Date: [DATE]
Vendor: [VENDOR if known]
My categories (use ONLY these names): [PASTE CHART OF ACCOUNTS — e.g. Rent, Utilities, Travel, Software, Marketing, Supplies, Meals, Legal, Contractors, Uncategorized]

Output:
- category: exact name from my list
- confidence: high / medium / low
- reason: one sentence
- needs_review: yes/no — yes if the description is vague, splits across categories, or looks personal

If it does not fit, use Uncategorized and set needs_review to yes. Do not invent a new category name.

setup.agent: Chat model for each receipt; optional Make/Zapier from email receipts into a sheet
steps: Export or type your chart of accounts into the prompt template.
For each receipt, paste description, amount, date, and vendor.
Run the prompt and write the category into your sheet or bookkeeping tool.
Queue anything marked needs_review for you or your bookkeeper.
Optional: forward receipt emails into an automation that fills the prompt.
setup.approvalStep: Review low-confidence and needs_review rows before month-end close.
failureModes: Inventing category names not on your chart
Splitting a mixed receipt into the wrong single category
Treating personal spend as business without a flag

toolPicks.whenNot: You have only a few expenses a month.

toolPicks.why: Self-hosted if receipts include sensitive data.
toolPicks.whenNot: You want a hosted tool only.

faq.q: What if it cannot categorize an expense?
faq.a: Mark Uncategorized and review with your bookkeeper. Do not force a bad fit.
No. It speeds sorting. A person still owns accuracy and tax treatment.
